# M3-2 — the rules baseline: results

*Generated by `./scripts/m3.sh -m m3 search`, which writes it to `ml/train/output/m3/M3_2_RESULTS.md` (gitignored) and it is copied to `docs/M3_2_RESULTS.md` — its canonical home, where the links below resolve. Do not hand-edit it: re-run the command.*

**Population.** 3 seeds (s1=20260818T185438Z, s2=20260819T142759Z, s3=20260820T025723Z), the 8-pair BASE8 universe, calendar span **252.7 days**.
**Protocol.** [M3_PROTOCOL.md](./M3_PROTOCOL.md), committed 2026-08-27 before this search ran. 36 primary configs + 1 sizing variant + 2 baselines + 1 O8 replication = 40 runs.
**Selection is at taker (14 bps).** Maker (5 bps) is reported alongside and never selected on.

```sh
./scripts/m3.sh -m m3 validate     # must pass first
./scripts/m3.sh -m m3 search
```

## A — The outcome

**1 of 36 primary configurations clear Tier 1**, and it is **`cov0.02_hold240_rqnone_mcnone`** — worst window **-3.56 bps** at taker (w4), pooled +8.03, 1,783 trades, all three seeds positive.

🔴 **Read what that configuration is.** No regime filter, no concurrency cap, no sizing: it is coverage alone. It is the row M2 already published in NEXT_TRAINING_PLAN §1.3 as the plain 2%-coverage slice, scored against fees and split by window for the first time. **Every configuration that uses the §1.8 regime filter — the finding this whole milestone was built around — fails Tier 1.**

They fail for the reason M3-1 pre-registered in §4.1 rather than for a new one, and the two strongest of them each fail **exactly one** of the six criteria — a different one:

| regime config | pooled net @14 | worst window | fails |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| `cov0.02_hold240_rq0.8_mcnone` | +18.3 | +10.1 | **P4** — w3 holds 45 trades, not 100 |
| `cov0.05_hold240_rq0.8_mcnone` | +9.4 | −2.5 | **P5** — seed 1 is pooled-negative at taker (−0.18) |

Neither is a P&L failure. The first is the sample-size floor catching a rule that fires unevenly across time; the second is the replication rule catching one that does not hold across seeds. Both floors were fixed in advance, from trade counts and from the §1.3 seed table, before any of this P&L existed.

**The sizing variant also clears Tier 1, and outranks the grid winner** (+0.25 vs -3.56 worst-window; +15.03 vs +8.03 pooled). The protocol does not say unambiguously whether an §3.2 addition may win the §4.2 ranking, so **both readings are reported and neither is chosen after the fact**: `cov0.02_hold240_rqnone_mcnone` is the baseline under the narrow reading, `cov0.02_hold240_rqnone_mcnone_SIZED` under the wide one. M3-3's bar (§4.4) is set at the stricter of the two, **+0.25 bps**, so the ambiguity costs nothing.

One caveat on the sizing variant that the ranking metric does not capture: it varies size, so its mean size is **1.337** and its per-trade mean is a size-weighted average. Per unit of notional actually deployed it is **+11.24 bps** at taker, not +15.03. §D1 carries that column per window.

**Tier 2 fails, as pre-registered (§4.3).** No candidate's clustered 95% lower bound is above zero, and §2 said in advance that this dataset cannot certify a policy at taker fees. See §E1.

| rule | criterion | passing |
|---|---|---:|
| P1 | pooled net at taker > 0 | 14 / 36 |
| P2 | net at taker > 0 in >= 3 of 4 windows | 12 / 36 |
| P3 | worst-window net at taker >= -5 bps | 4 / 36 |
| P4 | every window holds >= 100 pooled trades | 16 / 36 |
| P5 | all three seeds individually pooled-positive at taker | 4 / 36 |
| P6 | trade rate >= 0.5 trades/day/seed | 33 / 36 |
| **all** | **Tier 1** | **1 / 36** |

Three patterns hold across the whole grid and are worth carrying forward:

1. **`hold1440` is not tradeable on this evidence.** Every 24h-hold configuration loses catastrophically in w4 (−61 to −198 bps) whatever else is set. The 4h primary is the only hold the dump supports that also survives scoring.
2. **`hold60` never works.** Every 1h configuration is net-negative at taker: the edge does not cover a 14-bps round trip at that horizon.
3. **`max_concurrent=3` costs money everywhere.** Every capped config is worse than its uncapped twin, on both pooled and worst-window net. The cap is not selecting trades, it is dropping whichever ones arrive while three are already open — and on 8 pairs held serially the uncapped policy is a real 8-slot portfolio, not leverage.

## D — The three additions (M3_PROTOCOL §3.2)

They attach to **`cov0.02_hold240_rqnone_mcnone`** — the Tier-1 winner of the primary grid.

### D1 — the sizing variant

The anchor re-run with the hard regime filter **off** and size scaled 1/3..5/3 by the bar-quintile of `btc_absret_1d`: trade small out-of-regime instead of not at all.

```
config                             trades   net@5  net@14      w1      w2      w3      w4   worst in       s1      s2      s3 tr/day   maxdd sharpe  P123456  tier1
cov0.02_hold240_rqnone_mcnone_SIZED  1,773   +27.1   +15.0   +14.5   +19.2    +0.3   +15.1    +0.3 w3    +10.5    +9.6   +25.1   2.34  -4.586   0.93  YYYYYY  PASS
```

Mean size **1.337**, so the per-trade column above is a size-weighted average. Per unit of notional deployed (a diagnostic, not the ranking metric — see `per_notional` in `search.py`):

| fee | pooled | w1 | w2 | w3 | w4 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| maker5 | +20.24 | +20.28 | +22.44 | +9.25 | +20.09 |
| taker14 | +11.24 | +11.28 | +13.44 | +0.25 | +11.09 |

**The soft version of the regime idea is the one that survives.** The hard top-quintile filter fails Tier 1 in every form; scaling size by the same quintile while still trading out-of-regime passes it, and improves the grid winner's worst window. That is the concrete, actionable finding of M3-2.

Two things it costs, both of which belong next to that sentence. **Drawdown grows**: -4.586 against -2.761 for the flat-size anchor, which is what sizing up into volatile regimes buys you. And **the worst window is barely above the floor** — w3 at +0.25 bps on 192 trades is not a positive result, it is an absence of a negative one. The rule clears P3; it does not clear it comfortably.

### D2 — buy-and-hold, equal-weight across BASE8

Compounded from non-overlapping 4h legs of the same `fwd_ret` series every policy is booked against, so the comparison is like-for-like.

```
window  pairs  legs  eqw_total_ret  mean_leg_bps
    w1      8  2576        -0.1608       -4.1062
    w2      8  2832        -0.1417       -2.9123
    w3      8  2928        +0.3391       +7.8029
    w4      8  3736        -0.1393       -1.6556
   ALL      8 12072        -0.1308       -0.1900
```

The universe lost money over the evaluation period and in three of four windows, so every candidate above beats it comfortably. This baseline is a floor, not a rival.

### D3 — the momentum-side control

`cov0.02_hold240_rqnone_mcnone_SIZED`'s own entry bars, with the side taken from `sign(trailing 240m return)` instead of from the model. This isolates the one question that matters: **is the model's side worth anything over a trivial one?**

```
config                             trades   net@5  net@14      w1      w2      w3      w4   worst in       s1      s2      s3 tr/day   maxdd sharpe  P123456  tier1
cov0.02_hold240_rqnone_mcnone_SIZED_MOMSIDE  1,772    -9.8   -21.8   -18.3    +3.4   +12.0   -70.6   -70.6 w4    -13.4   -15.5   -37.2   2.34  -5.687  -1.70  ...Y.Y  -
```

**Model side minus momentum side: +36.88 bps/trade at taker** (+15.03 vs -21.84, over 1,773 vs 1,772 of the same entry bars). The control is net-negative in three of four windows and on all three seeds. **The model's direction call is carrying the strategy** — this is the single most reassuring number in M3-2, and the one that says the policy is not just a repackaged beta bet.

### E1 — Tier 2, the certification bar (M3_PROTOCOL §4.3)

| candidate | mean | clusters | n | SE | 95% CI | Tier 2 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|---|
| `cov0.02_hold240_rqnone_mcnone` | +8.03 | 162 | 1,783 | 16.97 | [-25.24, +41.30] | **FAIL** |
| `cov0.02_hold240_rqnone_mcnone_SIZED` | +15.03 | 162 | 1,773 | 24.53 | [-33.04, +63.11] | **FAIL** |

§4.3 pre-registered the expectation that Tier 2 fails for every candidate, and it does. A failure here is not evidence the metric is wrong; it is the sample size §2 measured, showing up where it was said it would.


Replication across *instruments*, not across time — same calendar period, four extra pairs, one seed. It is reported and was never selected on.

**How to read it.** The pooled numbers replicate and then some: each candidate earns *more* at taker on 12 pairs than on 8. The worst-window column does **not** replicate, and should not be expected to — O8 is a single seed, so its w3 holds 32 trades against the 192 the three-seed population has, and a mean over 32 trades at a 259-bps per-trade spread measures nothing. That is rule P4's threshold doing its job in a place where P4 was never applied: both O8 rows fail P4, which is why neither shows a Tier-1 verdict. The instrument replication supports the *pooled* edge and is silent on the robustness criterion.

## F — What this means for the milestone

A rules baseline clears the pre-registered Tier-1 bar. **M3-3's bar (§4.4): pass all of Tier 1 and beat +0.25 bps worst-window net at taker**, which is `cov0.02_hold240_rqnone_mcnone_SIZED`.

Three things follow for how the rest of M3 should be spent:

1. **The regime finding did not survive contact with the protocol in its hard form, but it did in its soft one.** Sizing by the regime quintile beats both filtering on it and ignoring it. A learned policy should be given the regime as a *continuous observation*, not handed a threshold to reproduce.
2. **Tier 2 still fails, so nothing here justifies size.** The honest use of this baseline is as M3-3's benchmark and as a paper-trading candidate — the forward paper-sim (§1 of the protocol) is the only genuinely out-of-time evidence available and it still does not exist.
3. **The maker column is where the leverage is.** Every candidate roughly doubles at 5 bps. Whether those fills are obtainable is ranked risk #2 and is measurable cheaply on the paper-sim stack (M3_PLAN §3.3) — it is worth more than any further knob.

## G — Per-configuration detail (M3_PROTOCOL §5)

Both fees, per window, per seed, per side, with the clustered interval, for every one of the 36 primary configurations plus the sizing variant and the side control.
